public_rationale: CoreWeave's filing for the quarter ended September 30, 2025 identifies useful lives as estimates based on historical experience and assumptions [e1]. This supports the narrow point that depreciation schedules depend on estimates, but does not establish that their empirical support is inadequate [e1]. CNBC reported on November 14, 2025 that CoreWeave's CEO said its A100 GPUs were fully booked [e2]. That later management report does not validate complete physical or profitable economic lifespans, leaving the stronger claim unresolved [e1, e2].
limitations: One company's accounting disclosure does not establish industry-wide adequacy [e1].
The booking report falls outside July–September 2025 and does not independently verify utilization or establish full useful lives [e2].

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Data center GPU depreciation schedules are based at best on assumptions and at worst on hope.

statement.excerpt: Any kind of depreciation schedule is based on, at best, assumptions, and at worst, hope.
statement.document_title: NVIDIA Isn't Enron - So What Is It?

our_interpretation: The surrounding discussion limits the claim to data center GPUs.
The ordinary reading is that useful-life schedules depend on uncertain projections of durability, obsolescence and demand. The context also questions how well those projections have been validated.
Merely showing that accounting uses estimates would establish the narrow reading, but would not establish that the estimates lack adequate empirical support.
Use July–September 2025, the latest completed calendar quarter reportable before publication, for the ongoing accounting practice.
Treat 'hope' as rhetorical emphasis, not a separately measurable assertion about management's beliefs.
criteria.support_condition: Accounting policies and supporting studies show that GPU useful-life schedules depend on projections whose full physical and economic lifespans remain unvalidated. Supporting the stronger contextual reading also requires evidence that the available empirical support is inadequate.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative engineering, retirement and commercial-use records establish the scheduled economic lives sufficiently well to contradict the suggestion that the schedules rest only on unvalidated projections.

evidence.locator: Note 1, Use of Estimates; related GPU useful-life discussion on page 69
evidence.explanation: The note includes useful lives among significant estimates, and the risk discussion expressly covers GPU useful-life uncertainty. This supports dependence on assumptions while also acknowledging an empirical basis.

This reported management observation provides counterweight to a reading that no empirical support exists. It neither independently verifies utilization nor establishes a complete useful life, and it is outside the target quarter.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative engineering, retirement and commercial-use records, alongside the studies used to set July–September 2025 depreciation schedules, would establish whether their empirical support was adequate. These records must distinguish physical survival, continued utilization and profitable economic use.
